posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: Well, it says it's a 50mJ laser, but doesn't give the pulse time. What you need to do is to find out the pulse time, divide out the power by the time and work out the energy delivered/pulse. Then you need to figure out what the rate of change of phase for your moving object is (assuming you're trying for a mving object). Basically, the phase must not change by pi/2 over the time of the exposure. The above figures will give you the amount of energy released in the calculated time of exposure. Knowing the sensitivity of the film, you now have the maximum velocity an object can move to be holographically captured by this laser.

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md: You might be able to shoot 8" by 10" single beam reflections with this amount of energy, certainly 4" by 5" no problem, if coherence is OK. This applies to practical experience with 8E75HD with SM-6 developer. I don't know how the current batch of materials take to that long lambda ruby light.

posts.content_md:
> I don't know how the current batch of materials take to that long lambda ruby light.

I heard of someone at a university in washington using a ruby to do inteferometry on PFG-01, but I think it was a 1 Joule laser. I also heard you might be able to record it (694nm) on PCG-03C, but haven't heard of much success with that on this forum.

I actuallly have one of these lasers, but haven't had the time to build it up. I bought it with the PFN and HV transformer and trigger.

I'm not sure if I want to try holography with it now 1) beacuse of the lack of materials to shoot it on and 2) because of the increased risk of personal injury! I've seen pic's of these lasers buringing holes in thin metal, etc. (That is actually the usage mode currently planned now if I can make the time. ) But saftey first, and I've got to get a HV relay to keep the PFN discharged, and a meter to monitior the HV.

Dave, would you shoot a Denisyuk with it, or try split beam? One thing to remember is these ruby's don't like heat and so have a very low rep. rate, like 1 pulse per second, so you I would think you need to take several test shots to get the alignment right. And if you want to do H1's with splitbeam, you probably need a HeNE or diode to help with alignment.
